items.stem: A user needs to run one administrative command without full root. What is the least-privilege approach?

options.text: Grant a scoped sudo rule for that specific command
options.rationale: Correct: a scoped sudoers entry grants only the needed command.

options.text: Add the user to the root group
options.rationale: Group membership can grant far more than one command.
Sharing root credentials violates least privilege and accountability.

options.text: Set the command setuid root for everyone
options.rationale: A world-executable setuid-root binary is a serious risk.

items.explanation: Correct: a scoped sudoers entry grants only the needed command.

items.stem: A host can ping IPs but not resolve names. Which is the most likely cause?

options.rationale: Correct: reachable IPs with failed names points to DNS resolution.
A routing problem would also break IP reachability.
Disk capacity does not selectively break name resolution.
Authentication is unrelated to name resolution.

items.explanation: Correct: reachable IPs with failed names points to DNS resolution.

items.stem: Which TWO steps correctly add persistent LVM storage? (Select TWO)

options.text: Create the logical volume and format it with a file system
options.rationale: Correct: an LV must be created and formatted before use.

options.text: Add the mount to /etc/fstab and verify it mounts
options.rationale: Correct: an fstab entry makes the mount persistent across reboot.

options.text: Mount it once manually and assume it persists
options.rationale: A manual mount does not survive reboot.

options.text: Store data on it before creating a file system
options.rationale: You cannot store data before a file system exists.

items.explanation: Correct: an LV must be created and formatted before use. Correct: an fstab entry makes the mount persistent across reboot.
